name: חיבור שברים אלגבריים עם מכנה משותף – av/d + bv/d (באנגלית)

functions.name: igcd2
functions.body: if q=0 then abs(p) else igcd2(q,mod(p,q))

questiontext:
Express the following as a single fraction in its lowest terms:

\[ \frac{{CT:0}}{{CT:1}}+\frac{{CT:2}}{{CT:1}}. \]

[[input:ans]]
[[validation:ans]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Equal denominators: add the numerators and keep the denominator, then cancel any common factor.
Step 1 — The denominators are equal
Adding algebraic fractions is exactly the same as adding purely numerical fractions. When the denominators are equal, as in this example, the addition is simple. All that is required is to add the numerators together and divide by the denominator:

\[ \frac{{CT:0}}{{CT:1}}+\frac{{CT:2}}{{CT:1}}=\frac{{{CT:0}}+{{CT:2}}}{{{CT:1}}}=\frac{{{CT:3}}}{{{CT:1}}} \]

(collect the like terms: \({{CT:4}}+{{CT:5}}={{CT:6}}\)).
Step 2 — Lowest terms
It may then require simplifying. [[if test="{{CT:11}}"]]The numerator and the denominator have the common factor \({{CT:7}}\); cancel it:

\[ \frac{{{CT:3}}}{{{CT:1}}}=\frac{{{CT:7}}\cdot {{CT:8}}}{{{CT:7}}\cdot {{CT:9}}} \]

Now nothing else cancels, so the fraction is in its lowest terms:[[else]]The numerator and the denominator have no common factor other than \(1\), so the fraction is already in its lowest terms:[[/if]]

\[ \frac{{CT:0}}{{CT:1}}+\frac{{CT:2}}{{CT:1}} = {{CT:10}}. \]

on_true.feedback: Your answer is not in its simplest form but is otherwise correct.
You don't add fractions by adding the numerators and the denominators. When the denominators are equal it is a simple case of adding the numerators: \(\frac{a}{d}+\frac{b}{d}=\frac{a+b}{d}\)
